title: A Chaetoceros bloom in the Western North Atlantic
content:
Abstract
The majority of work on the North Atlantic Spring Bloom has focused on the Eastern North Atlantic, repeatedly finding diatom blooms. In 2016, the NAAMES study examined the spring bloom in the Western subpolar North Atlantic using 16S rRNA amplicons of chloroplasts. They found a mixed community dominated by the picoeukaryotic algae belonging to Chlorophyta instead of by diatoms. Here we used phylogenetic read placement of the 18S rRNA gene to examine metagenome depth profiles from the Western subpolar North Atlantic obtained during the Geotraces GA02 transect in May 2010, a period of peak productivity. The most Northern station Thiolassiosira diatoms were abundant within a mixture of diatom groups but at two Northern stations the large centric diatom from the Phaeoceros group of Chaetoceros bloomed, along with Chlorophyta. Nutrient and phytoplankton progressions were similar to previous data from the Eastern North Atlantic where coccolithophores appeared after silicate was consumed and the diatom bloom ended. Microzooplankton included ciliates, dinoflagellates, Choanozoa, Amoebozoa, Euglenozoa and Cercozoa. Acantharea reads were abundant at subpolar stations. Reasons for differences between the phytoplankton dynamics in 2010 and 2016 could include differences in cruise latitude and timing, interannual variability, or a regime shift in the North Atlantic.
